careers.name: VLSI / Digital Design & Verification Engineer
careers.summary: RTL design, design verification (UVM), synthesis, STA, physical design and DFT. The highest-odds off-campus trunk for an Indian ECE fresher: large, growing hiring (NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Intel, AMD, TI, MediaTek, Samsung, Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens EDA, Arm, plus startups InCore, Mindgrove, Netrasemi). Proof travels as open-source RTL, UVM testbenches and a taped-out tile.

careers.name: AI/ML Hardware Architect & Accelerator Engineer
careers.summary: Computer architecture, accelerator design (systolic arrays, dataflows), quantisation, GPU/CUDA, performance modelling and ML compilers / HW-SW co-design. Fewer fresher openings and more often gated on an MS, but reachable by branching off the VLSI trunk once architecture + efficient-ML + a modelling project are in place (Google silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, Tenstorrent, SiMa, Krutrim).

careers.name: Design Verification -> AI-Accelerator & Low-Power Architect
careers.summary: Enter as a design-verification engineer (SystemVerilog, UVM, SVA, cocotb, coverage closure), the largest fresher intake in Indian VLSI hiring, then grow into AI-accelerator architecture and low-power design: dataflows, number formats, sparsity, energy modelling, UPF/DVFS. Verification of accelerator datapaths is the bridge. Built for an India-first start plus a German chip-design MS (TU Dresden Nanoelectronic Systems, TUM Microelectronics and Chip Design, Stuttgart INFOTECH).

project.linkedin_line: Closed functional coverage on a UART UVM environment, documenting every hole and the test that closed it.

contracts.title: A covergroup from a test plan
steps: List 5 features of a UART in a test plan
contracts.hint: A bin you cannot name a reason for is noise. Map every bin to a plan line.
contracts.success_check: Coverage report shows all 5 coverpoints with sensible bins

contracts.title: Crosses and holes
steps: Run random tests and find the empty cells
contracts.hint: Crosses grow fast: n x m bins. Use ignore_bins for impossible combinations.
contracts.success_check: A written list of every hole with its cause

contracts.title: Close the holes
steps: Tighten constraints or add a directed sequence per hole
contracts.hint: Change constraints before writing directed tests: one constraint can close many cells.
contracts.success_check: The coverage target is met and each fix is a commit

nodes.name: Reference models & scoreboards (DPI-C)
outcomes: Call it from SystemVerilog through DPI
Build a scoreboard that compares in order and out of order

project.title: dpi-scoreboard
project.deliverable: A UVM scoreboard calling a C fixed-point MAC model through DPI, catching injected rounding bugs
project.linkedin_line: Built a UVM scoreboard backed by a C golden model via DPI that catches rounding bugs.

contracts.title: Call C from SystemVerilog
steps: Call it from a test and print
contracts.hint: Types must match: int<->int, bit[31:0]<->svBitVecVal.
contracts.success_check: SV prints the value returned from C

contracts.title: A fixed-point MAC model
contracts.context: Reuse your Q8.8 type from the C node.
steps: Write mac(acc,a,b) in Q8.8 with saturation
contracts.hint: Decide rounding once (truncate or round-half-up) and use it in RTL and model.
contracts.success_check: C unit tests pass including saturation

contracts.title: The scoreboard
steps: Feed monitor transactions into a scoreboard
Compare DUT against the DPI model
contracts.hint: Queue expected values on input, pop on output; report mismatches with both values.
contracts.success_check: The rounding bug fails with a readable mismatch report

nodes.name: Power: dynamic, leakage, clock gating
outcomes: Compute dynamic power from activity, capacitance, voltage and frequency
Explain leakage and its temperature dependence
Apply clock gating and operand isolation in RTL

project.title: gated-counter
project.deliverable: A counter bank with and without clock gating, with a written power estimate for each
project.linkedin_line: Cut estimated dynamic power of a counter bank with RTL clock gating and documented the arithmetic.

contracts.title: P = a C V^2 f by hand
contracts.hint: Power is quadratic in V and linear in f; lowering V usually forces lower f too.
contracts.success_check: A worked table of 6 power numbers with units

contracts.title: Leakage
steps: List subthreshold, gate and junction leakage
Explain why leakage grows with temperature
contracts.hint: Subthreshold current is exponential in (Vgs - Vt): small Vt changes matter a lot.
contracts.success_check: A one-page note naming each mechanism and a fix

contracts.title: Clock gating in RTL
steps: Rewrite it with an integrated clock-gate cell model
contracts.hint: Never AND the clock in plain logic: use a latch-based gate so the gated clock has no glitches.
contracts.success_check: Simulation shows fewer clock toggles with gating

nodes.name: Power estimation & analysis
outcomes: Run gate-level power reports with activity

project.title: power-report
project.deliverable: An open-flow power report (OpenSTA) for a small design with simulation activity, top-5 consumers explained
project.linkedin_line: Ran activity-annotated power analysis in an open flow and explained the top consumers.

contracts.title: Activity from simulation
steps: Dump a VCD from a gate-level simulation
Compute toggle rate of 3 nets by hand
contracts.hint: Activity = toggles per cycle; a clock toggles twice per cycle.
contracts.success_check: Hand and tool toggle rates agree within 10%

contracts.title: report_power
contracts.hint: Default activity is a guess; real VCD activity changes the answer a lot.
contracts.success_check: A saved report with and without VCD

contracts.title: Top consumers
contracts.context: OpenROAD docs, power grid section for context.
steps: Propose one fix for the top block
contracts.hint: Clock nets and memories usually top the list; check them first.
contracts.success_check: A ranked top-5 with one fix each

nodes.name: Power domains, UPF & DVFS
outcomes: Describe power domains, isolation, retention and level shifters in UPF

project.title: two-domain-upf
project.deliverable: A two-domain design with a UPF file (isolation + retention) and a written power-state table
project.linkedin_line: Wrote UPF for a two-domain design with isolation and retention and a power-state table.

contracts.title: Power domains on paper
steps: Split a design into always-on and switchable
contracts.hint: Every signal leaving a switched-off domain needs an isolation cell clamping it to a safe value.
contracts.success_check: A diagram with every crossing marked

contracts.title: A first UPF file
contracts.hint: UPF describes intent; the RTL stays unchanged.
contracts.success_check: A UPF file that names domains, supplies, isolation, retention

contracts.title: DVFS in numbers
contracts.context: NPTEL Low Power VLSI, voltage-scaling lectures.
steps: Compute power and time for one task at each
contracts.hint: Energy = power x time; the fastest point is rarely the lowest-energy one.
contracts.success_check: A table of energy per task at 3 points with the winner

nodes.name: Number formats for ML hardware
outcomes: Compare INT8, FP16, bfloat16 and FP8 in range and precision
Implement a quantised MAC with scaling
Measure accuracy loss from a format change

project.title: fp8-mac
project.deliverable: An INT8 and an FP8 (E4M3) MAC in RTL with a Python model and an error table
project.linkedin_line: Implemented INT8 and FP8 MAC units in RTL and measured their error against FP32.

contracts.title: Formats side by side
steps: Tabulate exponent/mantissa bits, range and epsilon for 5 formats
contracts.hint: Range comes from exponent bits, precision from mantissa bits.
contracts.success_check: A table with range, epsilon and the 0.1 error

contracts.title: INT8 quantisation with scale
contracts.context: Reuse the PyTorch quantisation notes from the efficiency node.
steps: Quantise a weight tensor with per-tensor scale
contracts.hint: scale = max|x| / 127 for symmetric INT8; per-channel cuts error on uneven layers.
contracts.success_check: Error numbers for per-tensor vs per-channel

contracts.title: A quantised MAC in RTL
steps: Write an INT8 x INT8 + INT32 accumulator MAC
Check against Python on random vectors
contracts.hint: Accumulate wide (32 bits) and narrow only at the end.
contracts.success_check: Random vectors match the Python model bit-exactly

nodes.name: Dataflows & mapping
outcomes: Write a layer as a loop nest and reorder it
Pick tiling for a buffer size and count memory accesses

project.title: conv-mapper
project.deliverable: A Python script that enumerates tilings for a conv layer and reports DRAM/SRAM accesses per tiling
project.linkedin_line: Wrote a loop-nest mapper that counts memory accesses per tiling for a convolution layer.

contracts.title: A conv as a loop nest
steps: Swap two loops and confirm the same output
contracts.hint: Loop order does not change the answer, only which data stays close.
contracts.success_check: Two loop orders, identical outputs, MAC count

contracts.title: Stationarity
steps: Sketch a PE array for one
contracts.hint: The innermost loops decide what stays in the PE.
contracts.success_check: A labelled sketch for each dataflow

contracts.title: Tiling for a buffer
contracts.hint: Accesses ~ data size x reloads; bigger tiles mean fewer reloads until they stop fitting.
contracts.success_check: A table of tilings with DRAM access counts and the best one

nodes.name: Performance & energy modelling
outcomes: Build a roofline for an accelerator
Estimate energy per inference from access counts
Use Timeloop/Accelergy-style models to compare designs

project.title: energy-model
project.deliverable: An energy model for two dataflows on one layer, with a roofline plot and pJ/MAC per design
project.linkedin_line: Built a roofline and energy model comparing two accelerator dataflows in pJ per MAC.

contracts.title: A roofline
contracts.context: The roofline paper from the accelerator node.
steps: Pick peak MAC/s and DRAM bandwidth
contracts.hint: Intensity = MACs / bytes moved; left of the ridge you are memory-bound.
contracts.success_check: A plot with 3 layers placed and labelled

contracts.title: Energy from access counts
steps: Assign pJ per DRAM/SRAM/RF access and per MAC
contracts.hint: A DRAM access costs ~100x a MAC; data movement usually dominates.
contracts.success_check: pJ/MAC for one mapping with the breakdown

contracts.title: Compare two designs
contracts.hint: Report both energy and latency; one design rarely wins both.
contracts.success_check: A two-row table and a 5-line conclusion

nodes.name: Sparsity & compression in hardware
outcomes: Explain sparse formats (CSR, bitmask) and their hardware cost

project.title: sparse-mv
project.deliverable: A sparse matrix-vector unit model (bitmask format) with speed-up and energy versus density
project.linkedin_line: Modelled a bitmask sparse MV unit and charted speed-up and energy against weight density.

contracts.title: Prune a layer
contracts.hint: Prune, then fine-tune; one-shot heavy pruning hurts.
contracts.success_check: An accuracy-vs-density plot

contracts.title: Sparse formats
steps: Encode a matrix in CSR and bitmask
contracts.hint: Index overhead can exceed the zeros you saved at moderate density.
contracts.success_check: Storage numbers and the crossover density

contracts.title: Speed-up vs density
steps: Model cycles for dense and sparse MV
contracts.hint: Load imbalance eats speed-up: the slowest PE sets the pace.
contracts.success_check: A speed-up plot with and without imbalance

nodes.name: Verifying ML-accelerator datapaths
outcomes: Verify a quantised MAC array against a golden model
Write coverage for corner numerics (saturation, zero, NaN)
Read an open accelerator's verification environment

project.title: mac-array-dv
project.deliverable: A UVM or cocotb environment for a 4x4 INT8 MAC array with a numerics coverage model, closed
project.linkedin_line: Verified a 4x4 INT8 MAC array with a golden model and closed numeric-corner coverage.

contracts.title: Golden model for an array
steps: Write a NumPy matmul golden model with INT8 saturation
contracts.hint: Bit-exact means the same rounding, saturation and accumulation width as the RTL.
contracts.success_check: Random tiles match the golden model bit-exactly

contracts.title: Numerics coverage
steps: Cover saturation, zero operands, max/min values
contracts.hint: Random stimulus almost never hits saturation; you need biased constraints.
contracts.success_check: A coverage report with holes named

contracts.title: Read a real environment
steps: Find how NVDLA checks its convolution core
contracts.hint: Look for the trace-based test flow and the reference model boundary.
contracts.success_check: 3 written ideas and one applied

nodes.name: Power-aware verification
outcomes: Run power-aware simulation with a UPF

project.title: pa-sim
project.deliverable: A power-aware test suite for the two-domain design: shutdown, isolation, retention restore, with injected bugs caught
project.linkedin_line: Wrote power-aware tests that catch isolation and retention bugs in a two-domain design.

contracts.title: Power sequences as tests
contracts.context: Verification Academy low-power topics, power-aware simulation.
steps: Write a shutdown -> isolate -> restore sequence
contracts.hint: Order matters: isolate before power-off, restore before de-isolating.
contracts.success_check: The sequence test passes on the good design

contracts.title: Inject power bugs
contracts.hint: A missing isolation shows as X propagating into the always-on domain.
contracts.success_check: Both injected bugs are caught

contracts.title: Power-state coverage
contracts.hint: Transitions during traffic are where real bugs hide.
contracts.success_check: Every legal transition covered

nodes.name: Low-power accelerator architecture
outcomes: Reason about near-memory compute and data-movement energy
Combine sparsity, low precision and DVFS in one design
Read and critique an energy-efficient accelerator paper

project.title: lp-accel-study
project.deliverable: A 4-page design study: an edge accelerator under a 100 mW budget, with modelled energy and a power-state plan
project.linkedin_line: Wrote a modelled design study for a sub-100 mW edge accelerator combining sparsity, INT8 and DVFS.

contracts.title: Read Eyeriss v2
steps: Summarise the NoC idea in 5 lines
contracts.hint: Ask: what data moves less, and what does the flexibility cost in area?
contracts.success_check: A half-page critique

contracts.title: A 100 mW budget
steps: Pick a target network and frame rate
Allocate the power budget to MACs, SRAM, DRAM
contracts.hint: Budget DRAM first: it usually blows the budget alone.
contracts.success_check: A budget table that closes under 100 mW

contracts.title: Power states for the accelerator
steps: Define idle, low and peak states
Estimate energy per inference per state
contracts.hint: Race-to-idle vs slow-and-low: compute both.
contracts.success_check: A power-state table with energy per inference

nodes.name: Capstone: a verified, power-characterised accelerator tile
outcomes: Design, verify and power-characterise a small accelerator tile end to end
Report coverage, energy and timing honestly
Package it as a portfolio and MS-application piece

project.title: tile-capstone
project.deliverable: A GitHub repo: INT8 MAC-array tile RTL, cocotb/UVM environment with closed coverage, OpenSTA timing and power reports, a 4-page write-up
project.linkedin_line: Built, verified and power-characterised an INT8 accelerator tile with an open flow, end to end.

contracts.title: Write the spec
steps: Write a test plan from the spec
contracts.hint: A spec you can verify has numbers in it: MHz, mW, coverage %.
contracts.success_check: A one-page spec with numeric targets

contracts.title: Verify to closure
steps: Reuse the golden model and coverage
contracts.hint: Freeze the RTL for the sign-off run; log every waiver.
contracts.success_check: Coverage target met with a tagged commit

contracts.title: Timing, power and the write-up
steps: Synthesise, run STA and activity-based power
contracts.hint: Report misses honestly: a missed target with a reason reads better than a hidden one.
contracts.success_check: A report with measured MHz, mW and coverage against the spec

Present one closed-coverage project in 5 minutes

project.linkedin_line: Prepared a DV-specific resume and project walkthrough for verification roles.

contracts.title: A target list
contracts.context: Public careers pages of design centres and EDA/service companies.
steps: List 20 DV openings with job IDs
contracts.hint: Service companies hire freshers in batches; product companies hire through referrals.
contracts.success_check: A list of 20 openings with tools noted

contracts.title: The standard questions

steps: Fix them with a code snippet each
contracts.hint: Phases, factory overrides, sequences vs sequencers and coverage come up every time.
contracts.success_check: 15 answered, 5 fixed with code

contracts.title: The 5-minute walkthrough
steps: Script: problem, environment, coverage, one bug found
contracts.hint: Lead with the bug you found: it proves the environment works.
contracts.success_check: A 5-minute recording you would send
